_about: Hardware the tracker follows. products: home-lab / workstation machines with dated price points per market; accelerators: datacenter parts across vendors and countries with dated purchase estimates. Every number carries a source. Rental prices are automatic (pipeline/fetch_hardware.py); exchange rates too (pipeline/fetch_fx.py). The monthly price agent (pipeline/price_agent.py) appends new dated points; nothing is overwritten, so the history grows.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA H100 SXM
accelerators.notes: 2023 eBay peak above $40k; used units now sell for about $14k. Rental fell through 2025, then rose again in 2026.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA H200 SXM
accelerators.notes: Sales to approved Chinese buyers allowed from early 2026 with a 25% US revenue share; trades at about $48k in Hong Kong (Sep 2026).

accelerators.name: NVIDIA B200
accelerators.notes: Jensen Huang quoted $30-40k at announcement (Mar 2024); street price in 2026 is higher. Not sold to China.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA B300 (Blackwell Ultra)
accelerators.notes: Not sold to China; a B300 server traded there for about CNY 7M (~$1M) in Apr 2026, nearly double the US price.

accelerators.name: AMD Instinct MI300X
accelerators.notes: Citi estimate (about $10k for Microsoft, $15k for others); AMD has not confirmed it.

accelerators.name: AMD Instinct MI355X
accelerators.notes: Rumoured price (analyst expectation, July 2025); not confirmed by AMD.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
accelerators.notes: Transacted purchase orders just under $5.0M (Aug 2026); $8-8.6M installed with networking.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72
accelerators.notes: Estimates doubled in three months as HBM4 memory prices surged (Morgan Stanley: memory is about $2M of the $7.8M).

accelerators.name: AMD Instinct MI325X
accelerators.notes: No purchase price reported.

accelerators.name: AMD Instinct MI455X
accelerators.notes: Announced July 2026, shipping H2 2026, mainly inside the Helios rack. Bandwidth 19.6 TB/s per launch materials (datasheet says 23.3).

accelerators.name: AMD Helios rack
accelerators.notes: Futurum estimate, about 40% above NVIDIA's Rubin rack.

accelerators.name: Intel Gaudi 3
accelerators.notes: One of the few published list prices: $125,000 for an 8-chip kit (Computex 2024).

accelerators.name: Intel Crescent Island
accelerators.notes: Inference-only GPU with LPDDR5X; sampling planned H2 2026; no price or bandwidth disclosed.

accelerators.name: Google TPU v6e Trillium
accelerators.notes: Not sold; rented only on Google Cloud.

accelerators.name: Google TPU7x Ironwood
accelerators.notes: Not sold; rented only on Google Cloud. Large customers pay far less (one estimate: about $1.60/hr for Anthropic).

accelerators.name: AWS Trainium2
accelerators.notes: Not sold; rented only on AWS.

accelerators.name: Microsoft Maia 200
accelerators.notes: Microsoft's own chip, used inside Azure; neither sold nor rented.

accelerators.name: Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a
accelerators.notes: Published list price; sold directly, including to individuals.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72
accelerators.notes: About $3M per rack.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA H20 (China)
accelerators.notes: Cut-down part for China. US licence required from Apr 2025, allowed again Jul 2025 with a 15% revenue share; Beijing then told firms to avoid it.

accelerators.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000D (China)
accelerators.notes: Bandwidth set just under the export threshold; China's regulator told firms to stop ordering it (Sep 2025).

accelerators.name: Huawei Ascend 910B
accelerators.notes: China's mainstream domestic chip. US guidance (May 2025) says using it anywhere risks breaching US export rules. Rents are low and falling as newer chips arrive.

accelerators.name: Huawei Ascend 910C
accelerators.notes: Two 910B-class dies in one package. Price up over 20% in 2026 on the HBM memory shortage; about 600k targeted for 2026 (Bloomberg).

accelerators.name: Huawei Ascend 950PR
accelerators.notes: Mass production from Apr 2026, about 750k units planned for 2026; ByteDance and Alibaba plan orders. Price up about 30% since January.

accelerators.name: Huawei Ascend 950DT
accelerators.notes: Huawei's own HBM; heart of the Atlas 950 SuperPoD (8,192 chips). Quotes rose 20-50% in two months.

accelerators.name: Huawei CloudMatrix 384
accelerators.notes: About 3× the price of an NVIDIA NVL72 for similar total compute, using far more chips and power (about 560 kW).

accelerators.name: MetaX Xiyun C500
accelerators.notes: Average selling price per card from MetaX's IPO filing (excl. VAT): falling as volume grew from 272 cards (2023) to 6,649 (2024).

accelerators.name: MetaX Xiyun C550
accelerators.notes: Average selling price from MetaX's IPO filing (excl. VAT); rising in 2025.

accelerators.name: Moore Threads MTT S4000
accelerators.notes: Average selling price from Moore Threads' IPO filing (excl. VAT). On the US Entity List since Oct 2023.

accelerators.name: Enflame S60
accelerators.notes: Inference card, Tencent's main supplier; company-wide average price per card from Enflame's prospectus (64,890 cards sold in 2025).

accelerators.name: Cambricon MLU590
accelerators.notes: No card price published. Revenue grew from CNY 1.18bn (2024) to 6.5bn (2025); about 116k cards shipped in 2025 (IDC). On the US Entity List since 2022.

accelerators.name: Kunlunxin P800
accelerators.notes: Baidu's chip. No price published; about 116k shipped in 2025 (IDC).

accelerators.name: Alibaba T-Head Zhenwu 810E
accelerators.notes: Alibaba's in-house chip, mostly offered as Alibaba Cloud capacity; about 265k shipped in 2025 (IDC), second only to Huawei among Chinese vendors.

accelerators.name: Biren BR166
accelerators.notes: Two BR106 dies in one package. No price published; revenue CNY 1.0bn in 2025. On the US Entity List since Oct 2023.

accelerators.name: Moore Threads MTT S5000
accelerators.notes: Adds FP8; vendor-claimed specs. No card price published; Moore Threads' revenue rose 147% in H1 2026.
